input.brief: Write a short blog post for small business owners about choosing their first project management tool.

output.title: Your first project management tool, chosen calmly
output.subtitle: How a small business can pick a tool its team will actually keep using.

intro.hook: Start with the owner staring at a long list of tools and no clear way to compare them, then promise a short, honest method.

sections.heading: Start with the work, not the software
sections.angle: Describe how the team really tracks work today and where things slip, so the tool is chosen to fix a real problem rather than to follow a trend.

visuals.prompt: A small team's shared whiteboard covered in colourful sticky notes arranged in columns, in a bright, tidy office
visuals.alt: A whiteboard covered in sticky notes arranged in columns
visuals.caption: Look at how work really moves before choosing a tool

sections.heading: What a small team really needs
sections.angle: Reduce the feature lists to the few capabilities a small team uses every day, and compare the common kinds of tool against them.

sections.heading: Run a small trial before you commit
sections.angle: Explain how to test one tool on one real project with a few people, and what to watch for early on.

sections.heading: Make it stick with the team
sections.angle: Adoption beats features: agree a few simple habits, name an owner for the tool and review later whether it is helping.

visuals.prompt: Colleagues around a laptop in a bright meeting room, seen from behind, relaxed and collaborative
visuals.alt: Colleagues gathered around a laptop in a bright room
visuals.caption: A tool only helps if the team uses it together

conclusion.heading: Pick the simple option and review it
